D018-D016_h001.question:
It’s been maybe… I don’t know, a couple of months? Time kind of blurs lately. Ever since that car accident last year things haven’t really gone back to normal, but the last few months have been worse. I’ll be at my desk talking to a client about their policy, and suddenly it’s like I’m back there again—just these flashes in my head of the impact, the sound, the glass. They pop in without me wanting them to, sometimes mixed with these other awful “what if” thoughts that don’t always match what actually happened, but they’re just there, looping.

I feel on edge all the time. If someone walks quickly past my cubicle or appears in the doorway unexpectedly, I jump out of my skin. Same thing if my kids come up behind me too fast at home. I keep misplacing files, forgetting where I put my keys, losing my train of thought on the phone—it’s embarrassing because my job is all about details.

What scares me is I don’t really enjoy anything anymore. Even time with my kids feels sort of flat, like I’m going through the motions. I keep thinking that if my ex-husband had picked them up on time that day none of this would’ve happened, and I get stuck in that sense of dread, like the worst part is still happening somehow.
D018-D016_h001.options:
A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D018-D016_h001.answer: C & B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D018-D016_h002.question:
I’ve been feeling really on edge for maybe… I don’t know, a few months now? Time kind of blurs.  

I work at this café, and sometimes something small sets me off. Like if a customer suddenly reaches past the counter and their hand brushes mine, I jump so hard I almost drop everything. My body reacts before my brain even catches up. Other times, I sort of freeze and my head feels stuffed with cotton, like I’m there but not really processing what’s happening.

There are these thoughts that keep looping in my head, and I can’t tell if they’re just me overthinking or something else. They come out of nowhere—at work, on the bus, trying to sleep—and I can’t shut them off. I get stuck replaying certain moments and also imagining “what if” scenarios, and it makes my chest tight. I feel this heavy shame, like something is wrong with me, and I keep thinking I should’ve done something differently back then.  

I also catch myself blaming specific people for how things turned out, but at the same time I don’t even feel proud of anything I do now. Even when my manager praises me, it just feels empty, like it doesn’t count.
D018-D016_h002.options:
A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D018-D016_h002.answer: C & B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D018-D016_h003.question:
It’s been… I don’t know, a few months at least that this has really been bothering me. I work at a vet clinic, so I’m around emergencies a lot, and ever since one really bad case, it feels like my brain hasn’t reset.

At night I keep having these intense dreams. They aren’t always the exact same scene, but they have the same feeling—something awful happening and me not being able to stop it. I wake up with my heart racing and this sense of dread that sticks with me all day.

I keep going over what happened, thinking, “If I’d done this sooner,” or “If I’d noticed that sign,” maybe it would’ve turned out differently. I know logically it wasn’t just on me, but I can’t shake the idea that I failed. It’s like the terror from that day is still right under my skin.

At work I feel spaced out, like my head’s full of cotton. Simple tasks take more effort, and I put things off. When someone walks quickly past me or comes around a corner suddenly, I jump more than I used to. And there are these thoughts that repeat in my head—“You missed something,” “You’re going to mess up again”—that I can’t seem to turn off, no matter how much I tell myself to stop.
D018-D016_h003.options:
A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D018-D016_h003.answer: C & B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D018-D016_h004.question:

I try to push them away, but the harder I try, the more they come back, and I end up mentally going over the same details again and again.

Sometimes, especially when I’m tired, it’s like I’m not fully in the studio anymore. I’ll suddenly feel as if I’m back in…well, in that situation I’ve been trying not to talk about, and for a few seconds I lose track of where I actually am. When that happens, or even if someone just drops something loudly behind me, my heart just slams in my chest and my hands shake for a long time. I don’t calm down quickly; it kind of ruins the whole rest of the segment.

Outside of work, I’ve pretty much stopped doing things I used to love—yoga classes, dinners with friends. I tell myself and others that certain people are at fault for what happened, and at the same time I can’t shake this sense that there’s something fundamentally wrong or shameful about me. My thinking feels foggy a lot of the time, like I’m reading the teleprompter through a layer of glass.

A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D018-D016_h004.answer: C & B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D018-D016_h005.question:

A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D018-D016_h005.answer: C & B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D018-D016_h006.question:

D018-D016_h007.question:

D018-D016_h008.question:

What’s bothering me too is these thoughts that just pop in and won’t leave—images, “what if” scenarios, sometimes about work, sometimes about my family. They feel intrusive, and I end up going over them again and again in my head, trying to neutralize them somehow, but I’m not sure it helps.

D018-D016_h009.question:

D018-D016_h010.question:

D018-D016_h011.question:
I’ve been feeling pretty messed up for a while now… maybe six months, maybe longer. It’s all kind of blurred together.

Sleep is rough. I get these intense dreams, not every night but often enough, where I wake up with my heart racing and this heavy, scared feeling. Sometimes I remember bits, sometimes it’s just the same mood as… what happened before, I guess. I hate going into detail about it, so I usually just say I didn’t sleep well.

I’ve started organizing my life around not thinking about it. I’ll cross the street to avoid certain buildings, ignore group chats if I think someone might bring it up, make excuses to skip events. At work, if a project or conversation even vaguely reminds me of that time, I just shut it down or change the subject.

My view of things has really shifted. I catch myself thinking the world is basically unsafe, like something bad can happen at any moment, and that people can’t be trusted. I go over it in my head and keep coming back to a few specific people who I feel really screwed me over or should’ve stopped things; I get stuck on how it’s their fault.

I also get these thoughts that just won’t quit—like mental loops—that pop in randomly during coding or meetings. I wouldn’t say I’m doing any big rituals or anything, but I do find myself double- and triple-checking things—locks, messages, bits of code—because if I don’t, I feel really on edge.

And I’m angry a lot now, over nothing. Little things set me off—someone missing a deadline, noise from neighbors, a bug in my code—and I’ll snap or stew about it for hours. My coworkers probably think I’m just grumpy, but inside it feels like I’m constantly wound too tight.

A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Acute Stress Disorder
    D. Adjustment Disorder

D018-D016_h012.question:

During the day my mind gets stuck on things. A thought will pop in—about something terrible happening to my kids, or some mistake I made decades ago—and it just goes round and round. I know it doesn’t make sense, but I can’t shake it. I catch myself going over the same details again and again in my head, almost like I’m checking something, and it makes me restless and snappy.

I lose my temper over small stuff—noise from the neighbors, the TV volume, someone being a few minutes late. I never used to be like that. Since my wife passed, it’s like a switch flipped. My children come by, they hug me, and I care about them, but I feel…blocked. I can’t really feel it back, just this heavy shame and this sense that I don’t deserve their affection.
